questions.question_text:
A hot pie is left on a bench in a room at $18^{\circ}$C. Its temperature falls quickly at first, then more and more slowly, and eventually settles at room temperature.
Which model best describes its temperature $T$ after $t$ minutes?

options.why: This decays towards $0^{\circ}$C, so it ignores the room temperature the pie settles at.
A straight line falls at a constant rate and eventually predicts temperatures below room temperature.
A reciprocal curve is undefined at $t=0$, so it gives no starting temperature for the pie.

questions.solution_text:
The temperature levels off at $18^{\circ}$C, so the model needs the horizontal asymptote $T=18$.
A decay curve shifted up by $18$ has that asymptote.
$T=Ae^{-mt}+18$

questions.question_text:
A machine's value is modelled by $A=15\,000(0.88)^{t}$ dollars, where $t$ is the number of years since it was bought.
What is its value after $3$ years, to the nearest dollar?

options.why: Subtracted $12\%$ of the original $\$15\,000$ three times, treating the decay as a constant amount each year.
Used an index of $2$ instead of $3$.
Used an index of $4$ instead of $3$.

questions.question_text:
A sample of an isotope has mass $M=500(0.5)^{\frac{t}{8}}$ grams, where $t$ is the number of days since it was measured.
After how many days is the mass $62.5$ g?

options.why: Solved for $\dfrac{t}{8}$ and gave the number of halvings instead of the number of days.
Gave the time for one halving, which takes the mass only to $250$ g.
Used $\dfrac{1}{16}$ of the original mass rather than $\dfrac{1}{8}$.

questions.question_text:
The number of days $d$ to complete a job varies inversely with the number of workers $w$.
Five workers take $18$ days.
How long would $12$ workers take?

options.why: Found the constant as $\dfrac{18}{5}=3.6$ and multiplied by $12$ instead of dividing by it.
Found the constant as $\dfrac{18}{5}=3.6$ instead of $5\times18$, then divided by $12$.
Multiplied the constant $90$ by $12$, treating the relationship as direct rather than inverse.

questions.question_text:
A kettle of water cools in a room at $21^{\circ}$C according to $T=Ae^{-mt}+21$, where $t$ is in minutes.
The water starts at $96^{\circ}$C. What is the value of $A$?

options.why: Read the starting temperature straight off as $A$, ignoring the $+21$ in the model.
Added the room temperature to the starting temperature instead of subtracting it.
Gave the value of the horizontal asymptote instead of the coefficient $A$.

questions.question_text:
A cyclist rides in a straight line away from home at $8$ m/s for $30$ seconds, then turns and rides straight back at $8$ m/s, arriving home after $60$ seconds.
Which model gives her distance $d$ metres from home for $0\le t\le60$?

options.why: Measures the distance from the turning point rather than from home, so it gives $0$ at $t=30$.
Put the turning point at $t=60$, which is when she arrives home, not when she turns.
A straight line ignores the turn, so it gives a negative distance for small $t$.

questions.solution_text:
The turning point is at $t=30$, where the distance is $8\times30=240$ m.
The distance falls by $8$ m for every second away from $t=30$.
$d=240-8\left|t-30\right|$
At $t=0$: $240-8\times30=0$, and at $t=60$: $240-8\times30=0$, as required.

Read the first drop of $40$ as a constant decrease, but the drops get smaller each hour.
Used a base above $1$, which grows instead of decaying.

questions.solution_text:
At $x=0$ the brightness is $80$, so $k=80$.
$\dfrac{40}{80}=0.5$
Each hour the brightness is multiplied by $0.5$, so $b=0.5$.
$y=80(0.5)^{x}$

questions.question_text:
A colony grows exponentially according to $N=250b^{t}$, where $t$ is in days.
There were $250$ organisms at $t=0$ and $2000$ at $t=3$.
Which model fits?

options.why: Used the total growth factor over three days, $\dfrac{2000}{250}=8$, as the daily base.
Multiplied the index by $3$ instead of taking the cube root of the growth factor.
Treated the growth as a constant increase each day rather than a constant multiplier.

questions.question_text:
The number of subscribers to a new service is modelled by $S=900(1.4)^{n}$, where $n$ is the number of months since it launched.
The model fits the first six months well.
Which statement best describes a limitation of the model?

options.text: It predicts growth with no upper limit, but the number of possible subscribers is finite.
It cannot give a number of subscribers at launch, because $n=0$ is not allowed.
options.why: At $n=0$ the model gives $900$, so the launch figure is defined.

options.text: It predicts the number of subscribers eventually falls to zero.
options.why: Confuses a base above $1$ with a decay model; this model only increases.

options.text: It can only be used when $n$ is a whole number of months.
options.why: Confuses a continuous model with a discrete one; any value of $n$ may be substituted.

questions.solution_text:
The base $1.4$ is greater than $1$, so $S$ keeps multiplying by $1.4$ every month with no ceiling.
At $n=36$ the model gives more than $10$ billion subscribers.
A real service is limited by the size of its market, so the model becomes unreliable well before then.
